derivation: Pad centres extracted from board.svg: circle elements mapped through viewBox 0 0 27957 21193 -> 402x304 with the root translate(-42763,-28610). The 14.4px spacing is the 0.1in header pitch and is what identifies a header run. Group sizes 10+8 top and 8+6 bottom match an Uno R3. CHECKED 2026-08-27 against Arduino's own EAGLE board file (UNO-TH_Rev3e.brd, from A000066-cad-files.zip, CC BY-SA 4.0), read by tools/import_board.py from elements IOH, IOL, POWER and AD: all 32 pads pair by row and order, and after fitting the one scale and offset that separates artwork pixels from millimetres, the residual is a median of 0.005 mm and a worst of 0.008 mm against a 2.540 mm header pitch. The coordinates here are deliberately NOT replaced by the vendor's: they are in artwork space and must land on the drawing they are painted over, and 8 micrometres is not a correction.
assumption: Pad-to-label assignment WAS an assumption -- the documented Uno R3 silkscreen order with USB at the left -- and is no longer one. Every label was confirmed 2026-08-27 against the net each pad sits on in Arduino's own board file, with zero disagreements across all 32: D13 through D10 carry the SPI nets SCK, MISO, MOSI and SS because that is what they are on an Uno, A4 and A5 appear twice because the R3 repeats them beside AREF, and IOREF sits on the +5V net because the R3 ties it there. Pin numbers come from the simulator's own pinsl names and were not part of that check. One real difference the check did find, recorded because it is a property of the artwork rather than of the pads: board.svg is not uniformly scaled. The best fit is 5.6616 px/mm across and 5.6382 px/mm down, a 0.41% anisotropy -- 0.28 mm over the board's 68.58 mm width. Nothing here depends on it, and a future importer that assumes one scale for both axes will be wrong by that much.
